candidates.file: Bus Éireann buses KR219 (87-D-2219) & KE2 (2 VZJ), Super Crazy Prices supermarket shuttle, March 1994.jpg
candidates.author: D464-Darren Hall
candidates.description: Super Crazy Prices were a discount version of Irish Supermarket chain Quinnsworth and had a number of supermakets around the country. In 1987 the company opened up its largest in Finglas in the Janelle Shopping Centre which was a converted textile factory, at that time there were few large supermarkets in its catchment area and two Bus Eireann KR class buses were employed 6 days a week to operate a service to Cabra and Blanchardstown via Finglas West, the service lasted until the late 1990s when Blanchardstown centre opened up and car usage also grew and Tesco bought both Quinnswort and Crazy prices in 1997 and the rest as they say is history! KR143 was used for a similar store in Wexford Town.

candidates.file: First known animal tracks on land (24279487891).jpg
candidates.author: Mike Beauregard from Nunavut, Canada
candidates.description: This is super crazy_ the earliest known tracks of life on land ~515 million years ago in the Cambrian era. Look closely at this busy slab to see quite a number of trackways from two kinds of trace fossils. Models of the animals are above the slab. Found in 1983 in a quarry north of Kingston Ontario, were two (!!) types of hand-sized to foot-long creatures crawling around in numbers and visible on wet parts of windblown beach sand. Left is Climatichnites, the trackway left by a large sluglike animal and right is Protichnites, the trace fossil for a 16-legged arthropod. Makes you wonder what these critters were grazing on. And these are large, well-developed and highly-evolved animals with chronological room for even earlier creatures perambulating ashore. Redpath Museum, McGill University, Montréal, Quebec, Canada. Museum is geotagged. Allow me to promote the latest global geocience offering, a very, very, very informative, well-written and photogenic coffee-table book published by Nimb

candidates.description: Star Wars was first released in US movie theatres on 25 May 1977, and Return of the Jedi on 25 May 1983. These photographs are headed “Darth Vader came to school” in a photo book of Richmond Park School activities and events from the 1980s. Richmond Park School was located in Melville, Hamilton. The school opened in 1959 and was closed in 2004. The archives of the school are contained in Ministry of Education Hamilton closed schools records, currently being arranged and described by staff at Archives New Zealand Auckland Office. Archives New Zealand Reference: ABNW A1836 38b For further enquiries please email auckland.archives@dia.govt.nz Material from Archives New Zealand Te Rua Mahara o Te Kāwanatanga

candidates.author: Ethan
candidates.description: Classic wrestling shot (from the days of Tri-X 400 film) of André the Giant giving his "size 20" boot to King Kong Bundy . At center-left in the white, three-starred pants is Big John Studd while standing outside the ring at far-right is Hillbilly Jim . Referee Dick Kroll watches from the far left. In this October 21, 1985 tag-team match at Madison Square Garden , André the Giant and Hillbilly Jim along with manager Captain Lou Albano (unpictured) were the "face" team (i.e., the "good guys") while King Kong Bundy and Big John Studd and manager Bobby "The Brain" Heenan (visible under André the Giant's crotch in the background) were the "heel" team (i.e., the "bad guys"). The match ended in a double-disqualification. The kick occurs at 13:55 in this video recording , 13 minutes 40 seconds after the ring of the bell to start the match (although the fighting erupted before the bell). Color commentary for the television broadcast was provided by Gorilla Monsoon and Jesse "The Body" Ventura
